sentences.text: Klamelisaurus was a medium-sized sauropod dinosaur roughly 13 meters long, with its neck making up half of its total body length.
The holotype, which is the specimen the species is based on, preserves nine neck vertebrae and features unique plate-like extensions on the bones between the neck joints.
Its forelimbs were shorter than its hindlimbs, and the top of the upper arm bone lacked the overhanging circular process seen in some related dinosaurs.
Scientists found deep openings on the sides of the neck vertebrae, a feature not commonly seen in other sauropods.
Zhao Xijin formally named the species Klamelisaurus gobiensis in 1993 after a partial skeleton was discovered thirty-five kilometers north of the abandoned town of Jiangjunmiao.
After being transported to Beijing in 1985, the fossils found in the Gobi Desert underwent preparation and restoration.
The specific layer containing the holotype dates to the Oxfordian, approximately 160 million years ago.
This herbivorous dinosaur lived during the Middle Jurassic period in what is now China.
Gregory S. Paul estimated the weight of an adult form at six tons based on the available skeletal evidence.
Zhao originally classified the animal as the sole member of a new subfamily called Klamelisaurinae within the order Bothrosauropodoidea.
Later phylogenetic analyses suggested it belongs to the family Mamenchisauridae, a group of primarily Chinese sauropods that Moore and colleagues termed the "core Mamenchisaurus-like taxa".

Researchers have debated whether Klamelisaurus is the adult form of the earlier genus Bellusaurus. Gregory S. Paul suggested in 2010 and 2016 that Klamelisaurus might be the adult form of Bellusaurus, estimating its length at 15 meters and weight at 5 tons under this hypothesis. However, Moore and colleagues refuted this in 2018, noting that the Klamelisaurus holotype comes from older rock layers and the differences between the genera were not due to age. They also identified differences in vertebral pneumatic features that cannot be explained by age differences, and Bellusaurus possessed specific pneumatic features in dorsal neural spines and arches that Klamelisaurus lacked. Although bifurcated neural spines and wing-shaped processes on rear dorsals might vary with age, complicating the distinction, Moore and colleagues ultimately refuted the possible synonymy of the two genera, stating the differences were slightly older and not ontogenetic.
